definition.en: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) is a member of the World Bank Group that focuses exclusively on the private sector in developing countries to promote sustainable economic growth.
definition.hi: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) is a member of the World Bank Group that focuses exclusively on the private sector in developing countries to promote sustainable economic growth.

importanceInUpsc.en: The IFC is a critical topic for UPSC GS-3 under the External Sector syllabus, as it highlights the role of multilateral institutions in private capital mobilization. Understanding its operational model is essential for analyzing India's engagement with global financial institutions and its impact on domestic infrastructure and industrial development.

learningOutcomes.en: Understand the mandate and operational structure of the IFC within the World Bank Group.

learningOutcomes.en: Analyze the role of the IFC in supporting private sector investments in the Indian economy.
